newsitem.title: UK: Munich Re has no political risks in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re has no political risks in Russia.

text.p: German reinsurer Munich Re said it has not reinsured political risks in the Russian Federation, a new and developing market where it is gradually expanding.
Munich has concentrated so far on marine, travel and health risks, which generated around $8.0 million of premium income in 1995.
"We are taking a long term view. I am optimistic as to what will happen in the Russian Federation, but it will take time," Munich Re board member Hans-Wilmar von Stockhausen told Reuters.
The group has identified 30 to 35 insurers, out of 850 licensed in Russia, with which it does or may do business in the foreseeable future.
Through its Moscow office and in Munich, Munich Re is training local insurers and advising on regulation and technical issues.
"We have done a lot of the spade work...We are helping them in their endeavours to set up a proper insurance industry and avoid some of the mistakes made elsewhere," von Stockhausen said.
The growth of Munich Re's business volume in the area would depend on the development of the primary insurance market, he added.
